nodes.label: AMPM Platform Decision Brief
nodes.rationale: Three parts: the platform in one picture, eight sections on what the documents left open and the default taken meanwhile, and the decisions themselves (ten now, fifteen later, the assumptions worth a glance). Every default is marked so AMPM can overturn it, and the developer package sits behind the brief so AMPM need not read it to answer.

nodes.label: Platform lifecycle in one picture
nodes.rationale: Public website, demo or trial, subscription, hotel discovery, then a branch: a client who does not hire AMPM stays a subscriber and nothing is deleted, a client who does gets a wedding project, guests, the wedding day and closure. Green boxes mark the stages AMPM's documents mentioned without defining or did not mention at all.

nodes.label: Four experiences in one system
nodes.rationale: The public website, the client portal, the team workspace and the guest RSVP pages share one system, which is why permissions and visibility are designed once rather than per surface.

nodes.label: Open area 1 - Getting in and paying
nodes.rationale: The documents conflict on whether the client pays from the website or AMPM creates the account first, and say nothing about demo duration or what an expired subscriber sees. Default taken: AMPM creates the account and invites, the client pays in the portal online or by transfer, hotel discovery then opens, and expiry leaves read access with nothing deleted.

nodes.label: Open area 2 - Hotels and prices
nodes.rationale: The specification's data model has nowhere to store a price or availability, and previous clients' photos need permission. Default taken: seasonal rate cards with line items and a verification date, availability answered inside each enquiry rather than kept as a calendar, a rights status on every photo and video, and spreadsheet import for hotel data.

nodes.label: Open area 3 - How AMPM earns and what the client sees
nodes.rationale: Designed for the stricter case so either commercial model works: every price carries a client-facing amount and a separate internal cost, and the internal side never leaves the server. Clients see estimates, approved amounts, invoices, payments and the next milestone; vendor quotes, contracts and received invoices are never visible.

nodes.label: Open area 4 - Who logs in on the client side and who approves
nodes.rationale: In many weddings the parents pay and the couple designs, so the default splits owner, approver and viewer with a separate switch for who may see money, one approval per decision unless AMPM says two, and on-behalf recording only with a note or document attached and visibly marked as recorded for the family.

nodes.label: Open area 5 - Guests, RSVP and privacy
nodes.rationale: The documents never said whether a link is per wedding or per household, nor whether identity documents are needed. Default taken: load the guest list first and give each household a private link so nobody sees another family and nothing is duplicated, meal preference from everyone, allergies optional and visible only to hospitality, and identity documents only where a hotel needs them, never Aadhaar, because Indian rules restrict storing Aadhaar numbers.

nodes.label: Open area 6 - The wedding day and closure
nodes.rationale: Staff work in ballrooms and lawns with poor signal and nothing in the documents mentioned working offline, so the cue sheet, readiness checks and arrival lists read without signal and sync on reconnect. A function cannot go live with a required check unmet unless a named manager records an exception, and closure is a checklist verified against the data.

nodes.label: Open area 7 - Flowcharts and specification disagree
nodes.rationale: The client-portal flowchart has no hotel area although hotel discovery is what a subscription buys, and its Home countdown assumes every client has a date; the team flowchart has no home for the Hotel or RSVP teams and nothing before a wedding exists. Fix: a Hotels tab and a subscriber-without-a-wedding home page, the five phone tabs kept with the nine specification areas on desktop, and tracked requests with a conversation instead of the implied live chat.

nodes.label: Open area 8 - Technology and operations
nodes.rationale: Whether app meant native or responsive, hosting, recovery speed, channels, sign-in, size and website editing were all unstated. Default taken: an installable responsive website in an Indian cloud region with a second Indian copy recoverable to within fifteen minutes, email plus WhatsApp and SMS, authenticator codes for staff, and sizing for fifty staff, forty concurrent weddings, fifteen hundred guests and five hundred hotels.

nodes.label: Seasonal rate card with verification date
nodes.rationale: Room rate per category, venue rental per event, per-plate minimums for veg and non-veg, taxes and service charge, each verified on a date by a named team member and marked Stale after a configurable period, so a shown price always carries its own freshness; prices are indicative ranges and never internal cost.

nodes.label: Margin model with separate internal cost
nodes.rationale: Chosen over the transparent-fee model because designing for the stricter case keeps either commercial choice open: the client sees one price while cost, margin, vendor rates, quotations, commissions and negotiations stay server-side and restricted to authorised personnel.

nodes.label: Private RSVP link per household
nodes.rationale: Preferred to one wedding-wide link because the single link forces a guest to find their own name and needs a review queue for mistakes, while a per-household link means no duplicates and no family sees another. AMPM's answer moved this to per-side or one combined link, with the final structure still to decide.

nodes.label: Guest identity documents, never Aadhaar
nodes.rationale: Collected only where a hotel requires them for a wedding, passport, voter ID or driving licence only because Indian rules restrict storing Aadhaar numbers, held in restricted storage visible to named staff; the assumed thirty-day deletion after checkout gave way to AMPM-approved retention policy, which is still open.

nodes.label: Offline wedding-day operations
nodes.rationale: Required because staff work in venues with poor signal: essential wedding-day information reads offline and syncs automatically on reconnect, with conflict detection and a controlled resolution process.

nodes.label: Hotel-discovery subscription (Rs 50,000, one month)
nodes.rationale: One-time, one month from activation, configurable in settings, for hotel discovery only; renewal is a new purchase that restores access and data; after expiry the client keeps read-only access to saved hotel names and existing enquiries and nothing is deleted.

nodes.label: Demo reached by mobile OTP
nodes.rationale: Replaces a separate trial: a prospect signs in with a mobile number and an OTP and sees a limited set of locations and sample hotels with indicative prices. Duration and the exact hotel and location limits are still open.

nodes.label: Tracked requests and live chat side by side
nodes.rationale: Both are required: live chat on the home page for immediate questions, and tracked requests with conversation history kept distinct so a formal change request keeps its own approval history rather than being lost in a chat thread.

nodes.label: Eleven points still to confirm (AMPM's own list, 25 October 2026)
nodes.rationale: Demo duration and limits, demo sample hotels, payment gateway, one or two representative logins, staff roles and cost visibility, hosting and recovery, capacity, WhatsApp and SMS provider, privacy wording and retention, material-change thresholds, archiving and restore workflow. Two more from the design side: whether the client portal is also needed on the web, and which client-facing amounts the wedding portal shows. These block sign-off of the screen designs and data model and the drafting of the schedule and cost estimate.

nodes.label: Answer sheet for Q1 to Q10 (completed 25 October 2026)
nodes.rationale: One line per Tier 1 question with the decision, who decided and the date, so the record of the 25 October answers is readable without re-reading the question text.

nodes.label: Fourteen assumptions with the most business consequence
nodes.rationale: Surfaced separately from the full list of 98 in the assumptions sheet because each one changes the business shape: no self-registration, subscription grants hotel modules only, expiry never deletes, a project only from an accepted agreement, per-person guest counting, frozen caterer headcounts, settings never code, and the system built for AMPM alone. The answers confirmed all but one, which was not addressed and stands.

nodes.label: Q1 - Website or native app, and is offline use required
nodes.rationale: The flowcharts said app and the specification said responsive. A website reaches every phone on publication while native apps roughly double the front-end work. DECIDED: native iOS and Android apps are required, with offline access to essential wedding-day information, automatic sync on reconnect, conflict detection and a controlled resolution process; the final architecture is to be agreed with the development team. Still open: whether the client portal is also needed on the web.

nodes.label: Q2 - How clients pay for the subscription
nodes.rationale: A gateway merchant account takes one to two weeks to open, so the path had to be fixed early. DECIDED: AMPM creates the account or sends an invitation link, the client enters couple names, contact, tentative dates and preferred locations and pays online by card or UPI; payment must create a record, activate the subscription once and be reviewable by authorised staff. Still open: the gateway provider.

nodes.label: Q3 - What the subscription is
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: hotel discovery only, Rs 50,000 one-time for one month from activation and configurable in settings; renewal is a new purchase; expiry leaves read-only access to saved hotel names and existing enquiries with nothing deleted; no separate trial because the OTP demo serves that purpose. Still open: demo duration, and whether the demo shows one or two sample hotels per location across up to three locations.

nodes.label: Q4 - How AMPM earns and what money the client sees
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: hotel discovery is a separate paid service and the wedding management fee is decided by AMPM outside the app, never derived from the subscription; internal costs, margins, vendor rates, quotations, commissions and negotiations are never shown to clients; vendor profiles and service details appear only after AMPM is appointed; online collection of milestone payments is out of the first release unless separately approved. Still open: which client-facing amounts the wedding portal shows, and which hotel-assistance services beyond availability checks carry a fee.

nodes.label: Q5 - Who on the client side logs in and approves
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: only two nominated family representatives use the client portal, one from each side, chosen by the families; no other family member holds an account without AMPM's authorisation; cost and margin are never visible to them; AMPM may record an outside-the-portal decision when a note or supporting record is attached. Still open: one shared login or two separately authenticated accounts (separate recommended for security and audit history), and whether one approval completes a decision or both must approve.

nodes.label: Q6 - Staff roles, and who sees cost and margin
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: AMPM manages the system and controls permissions; staff access is restricted by assigned responsibility and department, so a department manager on a phone sees only their own sections; the named departments are hotel, vendor, RSVP, hospitality, production, project manager and senior authorised management; internal financial information is restricted to specifically authorised personnel. Still open: the final staff role list and which users may see hotel costs and vendor costs.

nodes.label: Q7 - How guests respond and what is collected
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: invitation links are issued per side, or as one combined link when AMPM chooses; the RSVP team imports or creates the list and sends the links; guests cannot see other households or the list and cannot edit a submitted response, corrections going through a change request or the RSVP caller; the two representatives see approved summaries and cannot edit; every guest is counted individually including children, with meal preference, allergies where required, rooming and travel where applicable. Still open: the final link structure.

nodes.label: Q8 - Identity documents from guests
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: collected only where a hotel requires them for a wedding, under AMPM's control, in restricted storage, visible only to authorised staff, and never Aadhaar documents or numbers; nothing is deleted automatically and retention follows AMPM-approved policy, to be confirmed before launch. Still open: retention period and privacy wording for identity documents.

nodes.label: Q9 - Hotel data, verification and photo rights
nodes.rationale: The first release is only as good as this database. DECIDED: Eva maintains the existing hotel data and updates seasonal prices roughly three times a year; hotel pages show venue details, rooms, photos and videos, a food and menu grid, approximate room pricing, package price ranges, indicative venue rental, approximate per-plate pricing, capacity, facilities and map location; prices are indicative ranges with a last-verified date and never internal cost; availability is checked by the team on request or when a hotel is added to a selection; previous clients' photographs appear only with permission; spreadsheet import is supported; about 200 hotels at the start.

nodes.label: Q10 - What is in the first release
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: the first release includes the demo, the subscription hotel-discovery workflow, wedding management after appointment, vendor selection, the client portal, department-based team access, RSVP, tracked requests, live chat and offline wedding-day operations; it excludes website editing, online milestone payments and GST invoicing; only Eva's authorised personnel may approve operational exceptions and that authority must be configurable. Still open: whether this scope launches as one release or hotel discovery launches first with the wedding modules following.

nodes.label: Q11 - Channels for clients and guests
nodes.rationale: WhatsApp and SMS registrations take two to six weeks and should start early. DECIDED: email and WhatsApp are required, SMS is proposed, and live chat is required on the home page; providers to be confirmed. Still open: the WhatsApp and SMS providers.

nodes.label: Q12 - Will AMPM staff edit the public website
nodes.rationale: DECIDED no: staff will not edit public website content through the app in the initial scope and the website editor is not approved, which removes the assumed editor, analytics and form bot check from the first release.

nodes.label: Q13 - How people sign in
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: prospects, demo users and clients sign in with a mobile number and an OTP, replacing the assumed email and password; there is no unrestricted self-registration because AMPM creates the account or sends an invitation; staff hold individual authorised accounts with role- and department-based access. Still open: the staff authentication method, with an authenticator app recommended.

nodes.label: Q14 - Hosting, backups and recovery targets
nodes.rationale: Assumed an Indian region with a second Indian copy, at most fifteen minutes of data lost and four hours to recover, with accounts in AMPM's name. DECIDED: hosting, backup frequency and recovery timelines are yet to be confirmed with the developer. Still open: hosting provider and region, backup location, recovery targets.

nodes.label: Q15 - How big the system will get
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: about 200 hotels at the start and roughly 20 concurrent weddings as the planning assumption, well below the assumed five hundred hotels and forty weddings, with multiple weddings and departmental staff access. Still open: staff count and largest guest count.

nodes.label: Q16 - Currency, language and invoicing
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: Indian rupees, English as the primary language, and the platform will not issue GST invoices, which drops the assumed GST invoicing and the second-language readiness on guest pages.

nodes.label: Q17 - Privacy wording and data retention
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: AMPM decides the final privacy wording and retention policy; retention and deletion require AMPM's approval, guest and wedding information must stay access-controlled, and wedding records are not deleted automatically. Still open: privacy wording and retention periods for leads, guest records and identity documents.

nodes.label: Q18 - Weddings across several hotels or outside venues
nodes.rationale: DECIDED yes: a wedding can involve multiple hotels and venues, confirming the assumption and keeping venue a per-function rather than per-wedding attribute.

nodes.label: Q19 - Room blocks and rooming rules
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: blocks by hotel, room category and dates; allocation and rooming are handled by the team rather than automatically; counts must support both room-wise and person-wise calculations with children included.

nodes.label: Q20 - Questions and messages in the portal
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: both tracked requests with conversation history and live chat are required, live chat on the home page and distinguished from tracked requests so a formal change request keeps its own approval history; more options may be added later. This overturns the assumption that tracked requests alone would do.

nodes.label: Q21 - Change requests and versioning
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: submitted, reviewed, accepted or rejected, then implemented and closed; a change to an approved item creates a new version for approval, so an approval always names an exact version.

nodes.label: Q22 - Vendors or hotels logging in
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: no vendor or hotel logins in the current version, keeping all vendor and hotel data inside AMPM's own surfaces; possible later.

nodes.label: Q23 - Client access after the wedding
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: read-only client access for three months after the wedding rather than the assumed twelve, then the project is archived with AMPM's approval; records are not deleted because archiving is a change of status and permissions, and later access or reopening is controlled by AMPM. Still open: the exact workflow for archiving and for restoring access.

nodes.label: Q24 - Feedback and archive
nodes.rationale: DECIDED: a short feedback form after the wedding and an archived state that preserves the records, as assumed.

nodes.label: Q25 - What counts as a material change
nodes.rationale: Assumed a budget line moving ten percent or more, or a date or venue change, with thresholds held as settings. DECIDED: thresholds must be configurable and AMPM will define the final budget-change percentages, date-change and venue-change thresholds and the approval rules. Still open: the thresholds and approval rules themselves.
